Full-window exploration rotated through: economic security strategy, partners and openness, coercion and sanctions, dependencies and supply chains, raw materials and energy, technology security, investment and ownership, industry and competitiveness, trade policy, infrastructure. strand_a.title: State subsidies, supply chain resilience, and geopolitics influencing firm strategies in a post-2020 context: case study of the German semiconductor industry
strand_a.summary: State subsidies, supply chain resilience, and geopolitics influencing firm strategies in a post-2020 context: case study of the German semiconductor industry. Drawing on interviews with semiconductor firms, we discuss the interaction between positive market dynamics for automotive semiconductors, customer concerns for supply chain resilience related to environmental risk, the effect of heightened geopolitical risk mainly concerning China, and European Union subsidy schemes which reduced Germany’s cost disadvantage. Conceptually, we integrate these factors into the global production network 2.0 framework by discussing how risks and the de-risking state interact with the market imperative and cost–capability ratio dynamics to influence firm strategies.

strand_a.source: Gospodarka Surowcami Mineralnymi - Mineral Resources Management
strand_a.summary: Strategic autonomy in practice: Ukraine’s critical raw materials, growth accounting and shift-share evidence, 2010–2023. This article examines whether Ukraine’s endowment of critical raw materials (CRMs) – here, graphite, titanium (ilmenite) and manganese – can support post-war growth while advancing Europe’s strategic autonomy. Second, a shift-share decomposition of CRM exports (2018–2023) shows a large negative competitiveness effect in global markets, consistent with wartime disruption, but a positive competitiveness effect inside the EU-27 despite a contracting EU market – evidence of selective de-risking toward proximate, trusted suppliers.

strand_a.summary: European countries should coordinate closely to bolster supply chain resilience and trade policy bargaining power vis-à-vis China. , Introduction: China’s dominance in green technologies poses a challenge to Germany and the EU The so-called China Shock 2.0 – a wave of high-tech exports – has put traditional German industrial sectors like automotive and mechanical engineering under pressure. Economic interdependence between the EU and China is becoming unsustainably tilted in Beijing’s favor: China’s trade surplus with the EU stood at EUR 360 billion in 2025.3 The political will of European member states to reduce strategic dependencies as part of a de-risking strategy – for example, in critical infrastructure and energy security – is currently at odds with geo-economic realities. The lack of (affordable) European alternatives, as well as high and complex supply chain dependencies, make diversification difficult in the short and medium term, particularly due to the significant costs involved.In this time of geopolitical change, Beijing also faces the challenge of maintaining economic sovereignty and independence.

ABSTRACT This article reviews how energy security is being reconceptualised and practiced in the context of Europe’s low-carbon transition, with a particular focus on Germany and the state of Bavaria, and on the role of circular bio-resources converted by thermo-chemical-conversion technologies. The results reveal three recent global tendencies: a slowed yet ongoing sustainable transition, increasing cost pressures, and growing national ambitions to achieve energy and resource independence.

strand_a.title: Dependent capitalism in Central and Eastern Europe: long-term trends and new shocks
strand_a.summary: This article examines the long-term consequences of the development strategies adopted by post-socialist economies in Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), which are characterised by large-scale inflows of foreign direct investment (FDI) and the significant involvement of foreign capital in transformational processes. It analyses how FDI has reshaped economic structures whilst creating a specific vulnerability pattern. Whilst supporting productivity growth, export expansion, and partial convergence, FDI has also deepened dependence on transnational corporations, external financing and international production networks.

strand_a.title: Accelerating fossil gas independence in Europe
strand_a.authors: Lukas Franken, Iegor Riepin, T H Brown
strand_a.summary: Recent price shocks have prompted calls to curb Europe's dependence on fossil gas imports, but the cost of this goal, and the consumer protection it affords, remain uncertain. Here we address this gap by imposing constraints on fossil gas supply in a European energy system model that co-optimises abatement across all gas uses at high spatio-temporal resolution. Cutting import reliance proves economically compelling: through savings in power generation and low-temperature heat in industry and buildings, Europe can halve its natural gas consumption for 16bnEUR/a, aligning demand with the continent's production capacity of 200 bcm.

strand_a.title: Cold War 2.0 and defence readiness
strand_a.summary: In the context of simultaneous rise of external threats through CRINK and the reprioritisation of transatlantic ally’s global posture, we study how a protracted low intensity conflict with CRINK would affect European allies’ preparedness to protect the security of the citizens and the integrity of the territory. As a worst case, we investigate the trade channel of geo-economic fragmentation in a Cold War 2.0 implying a complete cessation of trade with CRINK and a full blockade of Taiwan in an international multi-sectoral macroeconomic model featuring the defence sector and interlinking countries via global supply chains. Even this less kinetic conflict will create challenges for Europe’s security—challenges that will only grow more acute as the crisis worsens.

strand_a.authors: Frederik Dahl Nielsen, Stian Backe, Benjamin Mitterrutzner, Pedro Crespo del Granado
strand_a.summary: To achieve climate neutrality, Europe’s hydrogen strategy combines domestic green hydrogen production with green hydrogen imports, but the optimal balance remains uncertain. This study applies the stochastic energy system model EMPIRE, coupled with sectoral demand projections, to quantify how variable renewable energy source (VRES) deployment trajectories and hydrogen demand pathways jointly shape Europe’s import requirements. Results show that import requirements in 2050 could range from 7.5 to 55 Mton/yr, depending on scenario developments.

dynamic_shocks.title: A conflict or blockade severs Europe's access to maritime trade routes
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on maritime trade routes. Separate primary evidence shows that an armed-conflict escalation can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of maritime trade routes.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for an armed-conflict escalation.
Primary evidence contains 2 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
3 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on maritime trade routes for current or planned work.
An armed-conflict escalation reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Plan alternative routes and inventories for chokepoint disruption.
Coordinate naval and commercial responses with partners.
Prepare alternative routes and suppliers before a conflict closes a corridor.
watch_for: A shipping route or supply corridor closes.
Insurers withdraw cover for a region.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Well supported enough to watch closely, with contextual signals reinforcing rather than carrying the case.

page_guarantee.rule: New records update candidate reasoning; the shelf is re-decided each scan from recomputed maturity. No record takes a slot automatically.
page_guarantee.creative_reserve: Reserve = grounded runners-up + a creative reserve of relevant, uncontradicted hypotheses (distant, cross-domain, emerging, weak-signal or partially grounded), at least 18 and topped up toward 45, rotated across wow levels with weight on surprise. They mature into page competition when grounded.

high_order_inference.publication_policy: Stage 7 claim-native selection treats the reasoning layer as a future-hypothesis corpus. Candidate formation is broad; missing roles, thin evidence and unrun counter-evidence tests lower maturity rather than forbidding the hypothesis. Grounded candidates compete only within their wow 1-5 bucket. Each product reserves five public slots per wow level (25 maximum), displayed in repeated 5-4-3-2-1 order; surplus grounded findings remain reserve and weaker hypotheses remain developing.
high_order_inference.lifecycle_policy: Claim-native stock persists as page/reserve/developing tiers. Evidence is recomputed each scan; candidates can strengthen, weaken or move between tiers as new evidence arrives. Counter-evidence and falsifier results affect maturity and can kill a contradicted hypothesis, but an unrun challenge is not a ban on future-facing reasoning.
high_order_inference.candidate_search_policy: Missing-role and falsifier queries remain ordinary scanner discovery inputs and receive no admission waiver.
